long_biography.plain_text:
Beckham emerged from Manchester United's youth system and became a central figure in the club's 1990s success, winning six league titles and the 1999 Champions League. A midfielder renowned for crossing and free kicks, he captained England and later played for Real Madrid, LA Galaxy, AC Milan and Paris Saint-Germain. He became the first English player to win league titles in four countries.

His commercial career developed alongside football through long-running endorsements and licensing. The option negotiated when he joined Major League Soccer later enabled him to establish Inter Miami CF, where he remains a co-owner and helped shape the club's identity and recruitment. He also leads a Salford City ownership group and founded the production company Studio 99. The studio develops documentary features, series and commercial content for global platforms and brands.

The authoritative record supplies the distinctive Sir David Robert Joseph Beckham full name and exact birth date; Architectural Digest documents the same Beckham aboard a customized 40-metre-class Riva 130 Bellissima named Seven; YachtBuyer supplies the exact 40-metre, 299-gross-tonne, 2023 vessel match; and official sports, personal and club sources converge on the same public identity.

The authoritative owner input records David Beckham as a current owner from 2022, but no reviewed public source discloses the legal holding entity, beneficial ownership chain, acquisition financing or whether any interest is personal, joint, corporate or charter-based. The vessel evidence is used to resolve identity, not to make an editorial legal-ownership claim.

The input also records a current 28.49-metre vessel named M-Sea from 2021. Public reporting describes an earlier Riva 90 Argo associated with Beckham and subsequently replaced by a larger Seven, but the reviewed strong sources do not establish that M-Sea is the same hull or explain why both relationships remain current upstream. Forbes-first research found and verified a current dedicated David Beckham profile. It matches the exact football career, British identity, London residence, endorsement history, brand-business transaction, MLS option and Inter Miami interest, so a Forbes social proposal is made.

Sports is both the wealth-creation and current primary industry. Football produced the original salary and endorsement platform, while Inter Miami is now the largest documented single asset and Beckham remains actively involved in two professional clubs. Media production, consumer ventures and licensing are material but do not displace football as the dominant causal and current sphere.

Self-made — independent start is used because Beckham progressed through youth football and built wealth from playing, endorsements, licensing and investment. Forbes identifies working parents but no inherited operating business, ownership stake or material family-capital launch platform.

Founder is the most representative wealth relationship because Beckham helped establish Inter Miami, founded Studio 99 and retains equity-linked brand interests. His earlier athlete and endorsement income and later investor and operating functions remain important, but the approved relationship taxonomy has no athlete or licensor category and Inter Miami is his largest documented current asset.

Forbes reports a 26% Inter Miami stake and says the Mas brothers own at least 70% and operate the club day to day. The dossier therefore uses co-owner and founder, not controlling owner, and attributes only the badge, brand and player-recruitment work that Forbes specifically describes.

Salford City ownership changed in 2025. Beckham and Gary Neville are part of and publicly lead the new consortium, while other Class of '92 figures left the shareholder group. Brand licensing is included as a defining current tag because Forbes and Beckham's own site document repeated endorsements, a partial brand-business sale and an Authentic partnership that co-owns and manages the global brand. Individual promotional campaigns are omitted as transient.
